candidate: Stdlib seeded quasi-random search over run launches (kit-native, no version)
what: A declared search-space file plus a seeded random and scrambled-Halton point generator that launches each point through the existing run controller.
problem_here: The kit has no search command; any search today requires installing Optuna, and an unattended loop needs a sampler that harness code owns.
mechanism: Radical-inverse Halton sequence with seeded per-dimension permutations using only the random module; points validated against the space; each launched with expctl launch --seed --deadline.
evidence: Tuning Playbook prefers quasi-random search in exploration (https://github.com/google-research/tuning_playbook, checked 2026-11-11, Google authors); Optuna TPE and GP samplers are random for their first 10 trials (https://optuna.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/samplers/generated/optuna.samplers.TPESampler.html, 5.0.0); budget-matched study shows surrogate engages only at trial 11 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21641, 2026-06-19, authors measured). No direct stdlib-versus-Optuna measurement on NN training found.
maturity: Method from 2012 (random search) and 2017 (scrambled Halton recommendation); no third-party code needed; licence n/a.
cost: Small: about 100 lines plus tests; plain Halton degrades in high dimensions so scrambling is required; no attack surface.
simpler_alternative: Pseudo-random uniform sampling only (playbook says slightly less efficient).
reason: At 10 to 30 trials it loses little to model-based samplers and removes the dependency for the common case.
cheap_local_trial: Run 8 Halton learning-rate points of a 2-minute toy training script through expctl launch on the RTX 5090, repeat with 3 study seeds, compare best-of-8 spread with 8 Optuna TPE trials.

candidate: Default-first and capped agent-proposal queue (hybrid rule, kit-native)
what: The incumbent configuration is always evaluated first; the agent may add proposals to a queue that fills at most a fixed share of trials; harness code validates each proposal against the declared space.
problem_here: The unattended loop needs a rule for mixing agent hypotheses with a principled sampler without letting the agent drive the whole search.
mechanism: Queue with source attribute and hard share cap (start at 20 to 30 percent); invalid proposals rejected and replaced by the sampler; the sampler learns from all results; with Optuna this maps to enqueue_trial(params, user_attrs, skip_if_exists).
evidence: Hybrid CMA-ES plus LLM at 30 percent share was best of 15 methods; shares of 80 percent collapsed below CMA-ES alone; agent on a fixed space was worse than random (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24647, v3 2026-04-04, Freiburg authors, one task, 3 seeds). Default seeding explains the LLM warm start (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21641). Handing an agent trajectory to a numerical optimizer matched staying agentic, 0.570 versus 0.569 (https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12183v1, 2026-10-08, 2 runs per task).
maturity: Pattern published March 2026; reference code https://github.com/ferreirafabio/autoresearch-automl (MIT, 61 stars); no dependency needed.
cost: Low code cost; needs a tested validator; the right share for frontier models at small budgets is not established.
simpler_alternative: Sampler only with the default enqueued (current hpo.md rule).
reason: Best-supported way to combine agent proposals with principled search; keeps state and decisions in harness code.
cheap_local_trial: On a 5-minute toy language-model run, compare sampler-only against sampler plus 25 percent agent proposals at 16 trials and 3 study seeds, counting agent tokens.

candidate: Fresh-seed confirmation and budget split enforced by the harness (kit-native)
what: After a search, harness code re-runs the top configurations with seeds not used in the search and applies the existing paired decision rule; the budget plan reserves runs for this.
problem_here: The best of N single-seed trials is optimistically biased; in unattended mode nobody checks that the confirmation step happened.
mechanism: Budget ledger reserves baseline seeds plus top-3 times 3 fresh seeds before any search trial is launched; keep decision comes from the frozen evaluator on the confirmation runs only.
evidence: About 10 percent of HPO cases select a configuration worse than the default or first one (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.19540, AutoML 2025, LMU authors, tabular benchmarks, abstract); with 20 trials lucky and unlucky studies differ by more than retraining variance (Tuning Playbook). Repeating every configuration during search did not reliably help in a small 2020 RL study (https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.14604).
maturity: Practice already in references/uncertainty.md; enforcement is new.
cost: Spends roughly a third of a 30-run budget on confirmation; the exact split is a hypothesis.
simpler_alternative: Advice only, as today.
reason: Directly serves the top-ranked quality attribute (no kept result depends on a lucky seed).
cheap_local_trial: Replay any finished 20-trial toy study: confirm top 3 with 3 fresh seeds each and record how often the search winner stays the winner.

candidate: Stdlib synchronous successive halving over run launches (kit-native)
what: Rung-based promotion of the best fraction of configurations to a larger training budget, implemented over run launches.
problem_here: Could cut search cost on one GPU when early results predict final results.
mechanism: Rungs with reduction factor 3 or 4; each rung either resumes from a checkpoint or re-launches with a schedule fitted to the rung length; promotion by rank only when the gap exceeds the noise floor.
evidence: ASHA paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.05934, MLSys 2020, abstract) and Ray docs recommending ASHA over HyperBand (https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/tune/api/schedulers.html, Ray 2.60). Risks: about 15 percent of learning curves ill-behaved (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15657, NeurIPS 2025 D&B, abstract); short-horizon bias towards small learning rates (https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.02021, ICLR 2018); playbook says schedules do not transfer between step budgets.
maturity: Method from 2016 to 2020; no third-party code needed.
cost: Moderate; wrong promotions silently discard the best configuration; schedule handling per rung is easy to get wrong.
simpler_alternative: No pruning plus a divergence threshold (current default).
reason: Useful only where a pilot shows rank stability; must be off by default.
cheap_local_trial: On a toy run, train 9 configurations fully, then simulate halving at one third of the budget and count how often the true best survives.

candidate: Pilot rank-correlation gate before any pruning (kit-native)
what: Before enabling rank-based pruning, compute the rank correlation between the metric at the cut point and the final metric over completed pilot trials.
problem_here: hpo.md says to prune only after a pilot shows early scores predict final ones but gives no concrete test.
mechanism: Spearman correlation from logged curves using the statistics module; pruning allowed only above a declared threshold and when gaps exceed the noise floor.
evidence: Poor rank correlation across budgets is the documented failure of bandit-based methods (LCDB 1.1 https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15657; short-horizon bias https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.02021). No primary source gives a threshold.
maturity: Standard statistic; new as an enforced gate.
cost: Needs about 8 or more completed trials before it says anything; threshold is a judgement call.
simpler_alternative: Never prune at budgets under about 30 trials.
reason: Cheap guard that turns a vague rule into a measurement.
cheap_local_trial: Compute the correlation on the run logs of any past study in the experiments folder.

candidate: Feasibility probe before a full trial (kit-native)
what: A few training steps at the proposed configuration to detect out-of-memory or divergence before the full budget is spent.
problem_here: Failed trials are invisible to samplers, so out-of-memory regions keep being proposed; faking a score is forbidden by the kit.
mechanism: Short dry run records peak memory and loss finiteness; infeasible points are logged as rejected proposals and the space bound is tightened in a new study version.
evidence: Out-of-memory rates of 1 to 61 percent across methods decided rankings more than diversity did (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24647); playbook asks to adjust the space when many points are infeasible (https://github.com/google-research/tuning_playbook). The probe itself is not evaluated in any source.
cost: A minute per proposal; a probe can pass and the full run still fail later.
simpler_alternative: Record failures and narrow the space by hand between rounds.
reason: Protects a small budget from wasted runs without scoring failures.
cheap_local_trial: Probe 10 random batch-size and width points on the 32 GB card and compare predicted with actual out-of-memory outcomes.

candidate: Noise-floor stop rule and budget ledger (kit-native)
what: Search stops on hard caps or when no improvement larger than the noise floor has appeared in the last k trials; all caps tracked in one ledger.
problem_here: Unattended mode needs stop rules in harness code; Optuna's terminator module is deprecated.
mechanism: Ledger of runs, GPU-hours, wall time and agent tokens checked before each launch; stagnation test against the measured baseline seed spread.
evidence: Termination when optimisation gain falls below statistical error improves the test-performance and time trade-off (https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08166, AutoML 2022, abstract); optuna.terminator deprecated in 4.9.0 and due for removal in 6.0.0 (https://optuna.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/terminator.html).
maturity: Idea from 2021 to 2022; the proxy rule is my simplification.
cost: Low; a too-small k stops early on noisy tasks.
simpler_alternative: Hard caps only.
reason: Caps are mandatory; the stagnation rule is a cheap addition to test.
cheap_local_trial: Replay a finished study and report where the rule would have stopped and what was lost.

what: Hyperparameter optimisation framework: TPE, GP, CMA-ES, QMC and random samplers, pruners, storages, importance analysis.
problem_here: Model-based search for studies of about 30 trials or more, conditional spaces, importance analysis; already the kit's optional search module.
mechanism: Define-by-run objective or ask and tell; sqlite or journal storage; enqueue_trial for seeded points.
evidence: Release notes https://github.com/optuna/optuna/releases/tag/v5.0.0 (2026-09-07); TPE 0.9768 against random 0.9873 on a small language model (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24647, third party).
maturity: First release 2018; latest 5.0.0 on 2026-09-07; MIT; about 15.0k GitHub stars (2026-11-09) and about 15.3M PyPI downloads in the last month (https://pypistats.org/packages/optuna, 2026-11-11).
cost: Pure Python with SQLAlchemy; journal storage default lock fails on native Windows without JournalFileOpenLock; sampler seeds must differ across processes; UTC timestamp change in 5.0; open memory-growth issue 6777 for long TPE studies.
simpler_alternative: Stdlib quasi-random search for small budgets.
reason: Still the best-supported optional search module; hpo.md needs the Windows, seeding, start-up and deprecation fixes.
cheap_local_trial: On native Windows, write to a journal file from two processes with the default lock and with JournalFileOpenLock and record which one fails.

candidate: Optuna GPSampler with reduced start-up trials (Optuna 5.0.0)
what: Gaussian-process sampler with noise modelling and batch acquisition, stable in 5.0.
problem_here: Small continuous spaces at 15 to 50 trials, where TPE is weak.
mechanism: Matern kernel GP; n_startup_trials defaults to 10 and can be lowered; needs scipy and torch (CPU).
evidence: Official budget guidance up to 500 trials (https://optuna.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/samplers/index.html); GP-BO 0.432 against TPE 0.344 at 30 evaluations on Bayesmark (https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12183v1, tabular models, 2 runs).
maturity: Added in Optuna 3.6 (2024), stable in 5.0; MIT.
cost: Extra dependencies; pruning works only inefficiently with it; fit time grows with trials.
simpler_alternative: Quasi-random points for the first 10 trials, then TPE.
reason: Plausible gain in the kit's main budget range; evidence is not from NN training.
cheap_local_trial: 20-trial two-parameter toy study, GPSampler with n_startup_trials=5 against TPE and Halton, 3 study seeds.

what: Sampler that switches between GP, TPE and CMA-ES by problem type and trial count.
problem_here: Removes the sampler choice for users who do not know which to pick.
mechanism: Loaded with optunahub.load_module, which downloads code from the registry repository, branch main by default.
evidence: https://hub.optuna.org/samplers/auto_sampler/ and https://optuna.github.io/optunahub/generated/optunahub.load_module.html (checked 2026-11-11); OptunaHub paper in JMLR 27 (2026) by the maintainers; no independent NN-training comparison found.
maturity: Released 2024; registry active; MIT; over 30k weekly downloads claimed by maintainers in October 2025.
cost: Network and run-time code download; unpinned by default; needs optunahub, cmaes, torch, scipy.
simpler_alternative: A two-line rule in hpo.md: GP under 50 continuous trials, TPE otherwise.
reason: Only acceptable with a pinned ref; benefit over a simple rule is unproven here.
cheap_local_trial: Load with ref set to a commit SHA, then repeat with the network disabled to confirm the cache behaviour.

what: LLM-as-surrogate sampler ported to OptunaHub.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Sends trial history to a hosted LLM (API key required) to propose numerical parameters; categoricals fall back to random sampling.
evidence: The OptunaHub port scored 0.9882, worse than random search at 0.9873, with 61 percent out-of-memory trials (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24647); reproduction study finds its surrogate weaker than GP or SMAC (https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18891).
maturity: Paper ICLR 2024; hub port 2025; needs gpt-4o-mini or similar.
cost: Account, key, network, per-trial tokens; trial history leaves the machine.
simpler_alternative: Capped agent-proposal queue using the coding agent already present.
reason: Measured worse than random in the only NN-training comparison.

what: Regret-bound and stagnation evaluators that stop a study automatically.
problem_here: Stop rule for unattended search.
mechanism: Compares an estimated regret bound with an error estimate.
evidence: Deprecated in 4.9.0, removal planned for 6.0.0 (https://optuna.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/terminator.html).
cost: API will disappear.
simpler_alternative: Kit-native noise-floor stop rule.
reason: Do not build on a deprecated API.

what: Local web dashboard for Optuna studies.
problem_here: Human inspection of slices and importance after a study.
mechanism: Reads the study storage and serves a local page.
evidence: Release 2026-09-10 (https://github.com/optuna/optuna-dashboard/releases). No evidence that it changes training outcomes.
cost: Extra package; a local port.
simpler_alternative: expctl status summary.
reason: Keep the existing mention; nothing to add.

what: Exposes Optuna create-study, ask and tell to an agent as tools.
problem_here: Agent-steered search.
mechanism: MCP tools around a study.
evidence: Last GitHub release 2025-11-10, none since (https://github.com/optuna/optuna-mcp/releases); agent-as-driver on a fixed space is weakly supported (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24647).
maturity: Official organisation; about 84 stars per the earlier note; quiet for 12 months.
cost: Another server and permission surface; lets the agent tell results itself, which conflicts with harness-owned measurement.
simpler_alternative: Agent-proposal queue validated by harness code.
reason: The harness, not the agent, must report results.

what: Rust implementation of Optuna for very large trial counts.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Faster sampling and storage for tens of thousands of trials.
evidence: https://github.com/optuna/rustuna, release python-v0.2.1 on 2026-10-30, self-described experimental.
cost: Experimental; enqueue_trial behaves differently.
simpler_alternative: Optuna.
reason: NN training never reaches the trial counts it targets; update the version in hpo.md or drop the line.

what: Distributed trial scheduler with ASHA, PBT, PB2, BOHB and searcher wrappers including Optuna.
problem_here: Several GPUs or nodes, or population-based training.
mechanism: Local or remote cluster processes schedule trials; schedulers stop or clone trials.
evidence: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/releases (2026-11-04); Windows support is beta and multi-node on Windows untested (https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-overview/installation.html); security model allows code execution by any client that reaches the cluster, token authentication default for local clusters since 2.59 (https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-security/index.html).
maturity: First release 2017; Apache-2.0; very wide adoption.
cost: Heavy dependency and background processes with open ports; Windows beta; compatibility of OptunaSearch with Optuna 5 not verified.
simpler_alternative: Sequential trials through the kit controller on one GPU.
reason: No benefit on one GPU; keep hpo.md's narrow recommendation.

what: A population trains in parallel; poor members copy better ones and perturb hyperparameters, yielding a schedule.
problem_here: Hyperparameter schedules found within one run.
mechanism: Exploit and explore at fixed intervals with checkpoints.
evidence: PBT can fall behind random search over long horizons (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03225, RLC 2025, abstract); Ray replay does not reproduce results exactly (https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/tune/examples/pbt_guide.html).
maturity: 2017 onwards; implemented in Ray Tune and Syne Tune.
cost: Needs 4 to 8 or more concurrent members on one GPU; result is a lineage, not a re-runnable configuration; conflicts with paired-seed confirmation.
simpler_alternative: Tune the schedule family as ordinary hyperparameters.
reason: Poor fit to a single GPU and to the validity rules.

what: Bayesian optimisation platform with noise models, constraints, transfer learning and early stopping.
problem_here: Noisy objectives with constraints, or reuse of earlier studies.
mechanism: BoTorch models and acquisition functions behind a client API.
evidence: Release notes https://github.com/facebook/Ax/releases/tag/1.3.0 (2026-06-04) and https://pypi.org/project/ax-platform/ (1.3.1, 2026-06-09); no NN-training comparison against Optuna found.
cost: Python 3.11+, PyTorch 2.4+, JAX now required; legacy service API deprecated; API churn between minor versions.
simpler_alternative: Optuna GPSampler.
reason: Only if constraints or transfer learning become a real need.
cheap_local_trial: 20-trial noisy toy objective, Ax against Optuna GPSampler, 3 seeds.

what: Bayesian optimisation with random-forest surrogate and racing across seeds or instances; multi-fidelity facade.
problem_here: Deciding how many seeds each configuration deserves during search.
mechanism: Intensification races a challenger against the incumbent on a growing set of seeds.
evidence: https://github.com/automl/SMAC3 (v2.4.1, 2026-09-10; scikit-learn forest default since 2.4.0); SMAC scored 0.9778 with 36 percent out-of-memory trials in https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24647.
cost: Docs describe Windows only through WSL as experimental; ConfigSpace dependency.
simpler_alternative: Single-seed search plus fresh-seed confirmation of the top 3.
reason: The racing idea is worth borrowing; the dependency is not yet justified.
cheap_local_trial: Under WSL2, run its multi-fidelity example on a toy training script with seeds as instances.

what: Asynchronous multi-fidelity and transfer HPO with a local backend that runs trial scripts as processes.
problem_here: Multi-fidelity search over script launches.
mechanism: Schedulers such as ASHA, BOHB, CQR and PBT decide which trial process to start, pause or stop.
evidence: https://pypi.org/project/syne-tune/ (0.16.0, 2026-08-03) and https://syne-tune.readthedocs.io/en/latest/getting_started.html; no independent NN-training comparison read.
maturity: Started at AWS Labs in 2021, now under its own organisation; Apache-2.0; about 430 stars.
cost: Native Windows support not stated; its own process control would overlap with the kit controller.
simpler_alternative: Kit-native successive halving.
reason: Closest architecture to the kit, but two controllers for one run is a risk.
cheap_local_trial: Under WSL2, run the ASHA local-backend example with a 2-minute toy script.

what: HPO library built around expert priors and cheap fidelities; workers coordinate through a shared directory.
problem_here: A principled home for agent or user priors with multi-fidelity search and no server.
mechanism: Automatic choice: fidelity plus prior gives PriorBand, prior only gives piBO, fidelity only gives Hyperband; state lives in a results directory.
evidence: https://pypi.org/project/neural-pipeline-search/ (0.17.0, 2026-10-02) and https://automl.github.io/neps/latest/reference/optimizers/; wrong priors erase gains in a controlled test (https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12183v1), which is the case prior-robust methods target.
maturity: Freiburg AutoML group; Apache-2.0; Python 3.11 to 3.14; Windows in classifiers; 89 stars.
cost: Small community; torch-based; behaviour on native Windows not tested here; pruning risks apply.
simpler_alternative: Agent-proposal queue inside a quasi-random or TPE study.
reason: Only tool found that treats priors as fallible inputs to a multi-fidelity method and needs no service.
cheap_local_trial: Native Windows: 12-evaluation toy study with a learning-rate prior and epochs as fidelity; repeat with a deliberately wrong prior.

what: In-context learning-curve extrapolation used to decide which run to continue.
problem_here: Could replace rank-based pruning with a probabilistic prediction.
mechanism: A pretrained transformer predicts the rest of each curve in one forward pass.
evidence: 10 to 100 times faster and more accurate than earlier surrogates on three deep-learning HPO benchmark families (https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16795, ICML 2024, authors measured).
maturity: Package MIT, 20 stars, limits of 1,000 configurations and 10 hyperparameter dimensions, values normalised to 0 to 1 (https://github.com/automl/ifBO).
cost: Model weights and torch; no evidence on LLM fine-tuning curves; small maintenance base.
simpler_alternative: Pilot rank-correlation gate plus successive halving.
reason: Promising but unproven for the kit's workloads.
cheap_local_trial: Feed logged curves of a finished toy study truncated at one third and compare predicted with actual final ranks.

what: Open-source version of Google's black-box optimisation service.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: JAX-based GP bandit; also offers scrambled-Halton quasi-random search.
evidence: https://github.com/google/vizier: last release 2025-02-01, commits to 2026-10-20.
maturity: Apache-2.0; about 1.7k stars; no release for 21 months.
cost: JAX stack; service-style API.
simpler_alternative: Stdlib Halton or Optuna.
reason: No advantage on one GPU.

what: Differential evolution with Hyperband.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Evolutionary multi-fidelity search.
evidence: https://github.com/automl/DEHB: last release 2024-07-11, last commit 2025-04-25.
cost: Unmaintained dependency.
simpler_alternative: NePS or kit-native successive halving.
reason: Remove from hpo.md section 9.

what: Heteroscedastic evolutionary Bayesian optimisation.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: GP with input and output warping.
evidence: https://github.com/huawei-noah/HEBO commit list; PyPI page did not load.
cost: Unknown release state.
simpler_alternative: Optuna GPSampler.
reason: No evidence of a need.

what: Gradient-free optimisation algorithms.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Evolution strategies and portfolios.
evidence: https://pypi.org/project/nevergrad/: 1.0.12 on 2025-04-23.
cost: Extra dependency.
simpler_alternative: Optuna CMA-ES sampler.
reason: Targets far larger trial counts.

what: Cost-frugal hyperparameter search.
problem_here: Cost-aware search was not examined in depth.
mechanism: Starts from a low-cost point and expands.
evidence: Release 2026-11-06 (https://github.com/microsoft/FLAML/releases); method claims not checked today.
cost: Extra dependency.
simpler_alternative: Enqueue a cheap default first.
reason: Not evaluated beyond release status.

what: Original TPE implementation.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: TPE over a tree-structured space.
evidence: Release 2026-07-24 (https://github.com/hyperopt/hyperopt/releases).
cost: Duplicates Optuna.
simpler_alternative: Optuna.
reason: No capability Optuna lacks.

what: Cost-aware Bayesian search.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Pareto-region search over cost and performance.
evidence: https://github.com/imbue-ai/carbs commit list.
cost: Unmaintained.
simpler_alternative: Budget ledger plus Optuna.
reason: Unmaintained.

what: HPO and architecture search aimed at HPC clusters.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Asynchronous model-based search.
evidence: Release 2026-01-05 (https://github.com/deephyper/deephyper/releases).
cost: HPC-oriented.
simpler_alternative: Optuna.
reason: Wrong scale for one GPU.

what: Sweep controller with grid, random and Bayes search and Hyperband early termination.
problem_here: Only for users who already track runs there.
mechanism: Hosted controller hands configurations to local agents.
evidence: https://docs.coreweave.com/guides/sweeps/sweep-config-keys/ (the old docs URL redirects there).
cost: Account and network; run data leaves the machine; a second controller.
simpler_alternative: Kit-native search with optional metric mirroring.
reason: A service cannot be the keep-or-revert authority.

what: Benchmark code for nine HPO methods on a small language model, including the CMA-ES plus LLM hybrid.
problem_here: Reference for the hybrid rule and for a cheap kit benchmark task.
mechanism: Extracts hyperparameters by parsing the training script; fixed 5-minute trials.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24647 and https://github.com/ferreirafabio/autoresearch-automl (MIT, created 2026-03-13, 61 stars).
cost: Tuned to an 80 GB card; would need shrinking for 32 GB.
simpler_alternative: Implement the capped queue directly.
reason: Read as a design reference; do not depend on it.

candidate: optim-agent (PyPI package, Codex skill and Claude Code plugin)
what: Uses a coding-agent CLI as the sampler in an ask and tell study, with space validation and random fallback.
problem_here: Ready-made agent-as-sampler for very small budgets.
mechanism: AgentSampler proposes each configuration from parameter meaning and trial history.
evidence: Self-reported, one hosted frontier model with task context, 10 trials, 5 seeds: cumulative best-so-far error about 21 percent below TPE on MNIST and about 21 percent below random on CIFAR-10; without context it was close to random on both (https://github.com/Optim-Agent/optim-agent, checked 2026-11-11). At 10 trials TPE is still in random start-up; the README notes one benchmark used the test split in selection.
maturity: Created 2026-07-07; MIT; about 800 stars; no independent evaluation.
cost: Agent tokens per trial; agent is the driver, which the best third-party study does not support beyond small budgets.
simpler_alternative: Capped agent-proposal queue.
reason: Useful comparison point; evidence is the vendor's own.

what: A coding agent proposes the search space, sampler and pruner for a script; Optuna runs trials; the agent may revise the space between rounds.
problem_here: Precedent for agent-designs-the-space, harness-runs-the-search.
mechanism: Agent output is advisory and cannot override schema or measurement constraints.
evidence: https://github.com/RobertTLange/autotune README (MIT, 20 stars); no quantitative results.
cost: Needs Node.js 22 and Python; shows Codex only.
simpler_alternative: A space-proposal step in the kit's own procedure.
reason: Borrow the division of labour, not the tool.

candidate: Agentic Bayesian optimisation (Sara with the lenz backend)
what: An agent directs a Bayesian-optimisation backend it can inspect and reconfigure.
problem_here: Alternative design where the agent is the decision maker.
mechanism: Agent tightens bounds, switches acquisition functions and commits evaluations.
evidence: Abstract claims BO-level reliability without priors and gains from language priors (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00316, v2 2026-08-11, Meta authors); in a third-party benchmark GP tools did not help agents on average, 0.589 without and 0.538 with full GP tools (https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12183v1).
cost: Agent in control conflicts with harness-decides rule.
simpler_alternative: Capped queue.
reason: Mixed third-party evidence and no artifact.

candidate: Decaying, rejectable priors (DynaBO, piBO, PriorBand ideas)
what: Prior beliefs about good regions that lose weight over time and can be rejected when data disagree.
problem_here: Agent hypotheses about good hyperparameter regions are sometimes wrong.
mechanism: Prior-weighted acquisition with decay; surrogate-based check for misleading priors.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02570 (v3 2026-07-31, abstract, authors measured); wrong priors erased gains in https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12183v1.
maturity: Available through NePS piBO and PriorBand; DynaBO package not confirmed.
cost: Needs a model-based optimizer.
simpler_alternative: Treat agent beliefs as proposals in the capped queue and never narrow the space on belief alone.
reason: The rule matters more than the algorithm at small budgets.
cheap_local_trial: Covered by the NePS trial with a wrong prior.

what: Benchmarks of agents as sequential hyperparameter or black-box optimizers.
problem_here: A cheap way to measure whether the kit helps an agent search.
mechanism: AgentHPOBench: 30 repository-level tasks, one baseline run plus five interventions. AgenticBBO-Bench: five domains, 25 to 30 evaluations.
evidence: https://github.com/OpenMOSS/AgentHPOBench (arXiv 2607.29626, Apache-2.0) and https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12183.
cost: Task set-up and GPU time; numeric results of the first not read.
simpler_alternative: Two or three in-house toy tasks.
reason: The baseline-plus-five protocol matches how the kit is used.
cheap_local_trial: Pick two of the smallest tasks and run the protocol with and without the kit.

what: Open implementation of evolutionary program search with LLM mutation, MAP-Elites and islands.
problem_here: Population search over training code.
mechanism: Archive of programs scored by an evaluator script.
evidence: https://github.com/algorithmicsuperintelligence/openevolve (v0.4.1, 2026-11-02); examples use 50 to 460 iterations and none trains a neural network.
cost: Hundreds of evaluations and LLM calls; its own evaluator contract would sit beside the frozen evaluator.
simpler_alternative: The kit's keep-or-revert loop with a small archive of rejected ideas.
reason: Needs cheap evaluations the kit's workloads do not have.

what: Evolutionary program search with an ensemble of LLMs as mutation operators.
problem_here: Same as OpenEvolve.
mechanism: Islands, archive, evaluate script returning a combined score.
evidence: https://github.com/SakanaAI/ShinkaEvolve (v0.0.7, 2026-06-02); no neural-network-training example.
cost: Several LLM provider keys by default.
simpler_alternative: Keep-or-revert loop.
reason: Same mismatch with slow, noisy scorers.

candidate: AgileRL evolutionary HPO for LLM post-training
what: Population whose hyperparameters evolve during one training run, including SFT and RL fine-tuning of LLMs.
problem_here: Schedule search during fine-tuning.
mechanism: Population training with selection and mutation.
evidence: https://github.com/AgileRL/AgileRL README; speed claims are the project's own.
cost: Replaces the training loop; population on one GPU.
simpler_alternative: Ordinary tuning of learning rate and schedule.
reason: Framework lock-in and no independent evidence.

candidate: Per-arm learning-rate sweep rule for fine-tuning comparisons (dated advice, 2026)
what: When comparing fine-tuning methods, sweep the learning rate separately for each arm and treat batch size as a nuisance parameter.
problem_here: An agent comparing a LoRA variant with a baseline at one shared learning rate reports a false gain.
mechanism: Small log-scale learning-rate sweep per arm at fixed update count before any comparison.
evidence: Ten LoRA methods end within 1 to 2 percent once the learning rate is tuned, each preferring a different range (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04998, v2 2026-05-19, abstract); batch size explains conflicting LoRA results (https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09492, v2 2026-06-01, abstract).
maturity: Two 2026 preprints, one reported as accepted at a major venue by a search summary (not confirmed).
cost: Multiplies trials per arm.
simpler_alternative: Existing hpo.md line that the baseline deserves an equally tuned learning rate.
reason: Enters as dated, sourced advice that sharpens an existing rule and corrects the batch-size line for fine-tuning.
cheap_local_trial: LoRA on a small model with two ranks and five learning rates each; check whether the ranking at a shared learning rate differs from the ranking at each arm's best.

candidate: Data-subset fidelity for LoRA search (dated hypothesis, 2026)
what: Search LoRA hyperparameters on a data subset, then confirm on full data.
problem_here: Cuts the cost of fine-tuning searches on one GPU.
mechanism: Subset training as the cheap fidelity; top configurations re-run on full data.
evidence: Strong correlation between subset and full-data LoRA performance reported in https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11171 (abstract, authors measured).
cost: Correlation may not hold for small or shifted subsets.
simpler_alternative: Full-data search with fewer trials.
reason: Cheap to test with the rank-correlation gate.
cheap_local_trial: Train 6 LoRA configurations on 10 percent and 100 percent of a small dataset and compute the rank correlation.

what: An LLM trained to rank architecture, hyperparameter and data-ratio configurations.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: Trained searcher over encoded configurations.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12791 (2026-11-09, abstract); one experiment used 896 GPU-days.
cost: Far beyond a single GPU.
simpler_alternative: none needed
reason: Out of scale and unverifiable.
